meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'полнять'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to perform', paired with 'исполнить'.

examples.text: Это слово «исполнять» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'to perform' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!
Very well! Have a pleasant evening.

meanings.note: до вечера = until the evening; вечером = in the evening

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.
Thank you, Marina. Sorry, I'm in a hurry.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)

examples.trans: But apparently I came in vain.
He seems to have had too much.
The wind is blowing hard outside.

examples.text: Я так два года потеряла. Любила так сильно!
examples.trans: I lost two years like that. I loved him so much!

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'кушаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to get drunk, to overeat', paired with 'накушиваться'.

examples.trans: He seems to have had too much.

examples.text: Это слово «накушаться» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'to get drunk' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: Core Russian part meaning 'even' in everyday speech.
наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

examples.text: Настоящий повар чувствует каждый вкус блюда.
examples.trans: A real chef feels every taste of the dish.

examples.text: Осталось ровно три минуты до готовности блюда.
examples.trans: Exactly three minutes remain until the dish is ready.
The chef prepared a delicious dish.
I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: to get tired, to grow weary
meanings.note: past tense устал / устала often means 'am/is tired'

examples.trans: I am very tired of sitting.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'этому').

examples.text: Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: That's why I'm running for a second term.
I'm tired, so I'm at home.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.note: Borrowed from Latin agent/instrument noun in '-tor' ('дегустатор'). Common masculine noun meaning 'taster' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Then I will be the taster.

examples.text: Это слово «дегустатор» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'taster' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.en: to try, to taste (food or drink)

examples.trans: Try the tea with bread rings.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'деяться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hope, to rely on', paired with 'понадеяться'.

examples.trans: I hope so. Go on, act quickly!

meanings.en: to have a look, to take a look

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

приготовить.gloss: to prepare, to cook, to make

meanings.en: to cook, to make (food), to prepare

examples.text: Я торт приготовила. Ты любишь сладкое?
examples.trans: I made a cake. Do you have a sweet tooth?

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Я хочу работать поваром в ресторане.
examples.trans: I want to work as a cook in a restaurant.
